summary: HOT-SPOT is a web application that harmonizes active-fire hot spot detections from NASA's MODIS (Terra/Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20/21) sensors into a single, consistent active fire calendar. Fire data have been collected for more than twenty years, but the two sensors differ in resolution, detection sensitivity and overpass times, so their records are not directly comparable. HOT-SPOT aligns both sources so that early warning services, emergency responders, scientists and land managers can explore the fire history of any area of interest, identify critical burning periods and spot unusual conditions. An AI assistant, available in text and voice, helps users query the data and understand the results without technical expertise. Built by team Dev241 in Libreville, Gabon, HOT-SPOT aims to make satellite fire data actionable for anticipating fire seasons, guiding surveillance and protecting forests and communities.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

HOT-SPOT is a web application that brings together active-fire detections from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS sensors and harmonizes them into one consistent active fire calendar. Users select an area of interest and a time period, and HOT-SPOT shows when and where fires occurred, the critical burning periods of the year, and unusual conditions compared with the historical record.

HOW IT WORKS

MODIS (1 km resolution, since 2000) and VIIRS (375 m resolution, since 2012) detect fires differently. HOT-SPOT retrieves hot spot data from NASA FIRMS, normalizes the two sources to a common spatial and temporal grid, and aggregates detections into daily, monthly and seasonal views so the long MODIS record and the more detailed VIIRS record can be compared and used together.

AI ASSISTANT

An AI assistant, available in text and voice, lets users ask questions in natural language (for example: when is the peak fire season in this province?) and explains the results, making satellite data accessible to non-specialists.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

HOT-SPOT helps early warning and emergency services anticipate critical periods, helps land and forest managers target surveillance and prevention, and gives scientists a consistent multi-sensor fire history. Our team, based in Gabon, a country covered largely by tropical forest, designed it with Central African needs in mind: simple interfaces, voice interaction and clear visual calendars.

CREATIVITY

HOT-SPOT combines data harmonization, a calendar-based visualization of fire activity and a conversational AI assistant, turning two separate satellite archives into an actionable tool.
